thread:
anya: Quick flag — after the kernel-autoselect roll yesterday we're seeing a perf regression on multi-GPU for the chat benchmark. latency p50 up ~12% and tail spikes. Nsight capture shows long idle gaps between compute and all-reduce. anyone else? :eyes:
sam: Yep saw that on my run this morning. Can you share the trace + minimal repro?
anya: Putting quick repro steps below. Nsight capture attached in thread (will upload). Short repro: 4xA100, tp=2, pp=1, batch=8, seq=2048. Command: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --output=chat_trace python -m perf.chat_repro`
leo: Interesting. Any custom timers/nvtx ranges around KV cache or batching?
tess: I added a couple of timers yesterday around KV cache handshake and allreduce. Snip from our quick timer output:```
KVCACHE_PREFETCH: 0.78ms
KVCACHE_LOCK_WAIT: 0.30ms
ALLREDUCE_POST_ENQUEUE: 4.21ms
COMM_IDLE_GAP: 12.54ms
```
anya: Those numbers align with the nsight waterfall — compute finishes, then ~10-13ms idle, then large allreduce spikes. Looks like kernel-autopick picked a kernel variant that serializes better locally but hurts comm/compute overlap.
sam: Hypothesis: kernel-autoselect chose a different block/grid tiling that increases per-chunk enqueue latency and prevents async NCCL overlap. Could also be batching heuristic changed microbatch boundaries.
leo: Can we reproduce with kernel-autopick=off? Try `RUNTIME_KERNEL_AUTOPICK=0` env and re-run nsight. If performance > baseline, autoselect logic to blame.
tess: Will run both toggles: `RUNTIME_KERNEL_AUTOPICK=0` and `RUNTIME_BATCH_THRESHOLD=4` (we had bumped threshold up last week). Also enabling NCCL debug: `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=COLL` to get op timing.
anya: Also add NVTX markers around NCCL ops so nsight shows them:```
nvtxRangePush("allreduce_start");
ncclAllReduce(...);
nvtxRangePop();
```
leo: I'll instrument the kernel picker to log chosen kernel id + reason for selection (sequence length, batch, quantization). That should help correlate picks with traces.
sam: Small repro suggestion: reduce seq to 512 and microbatch to 2 to see whether overlap improves. If so, autotuner thresholds likely wrong for long sequences.
anya: One more datapoint: when I force the alternative kernel (old kernel id 0x7f), allreduce latency drops ~3ms and idle gap disappears in nsight. So it's plausible picker changed preference.
tess: Action items:
- leo: add kernel pick logging and a toggle to pin kernel id (due EOD)
- tess: run two nsight captures (autopick ON/OFF) + NCCL debug and upload traces
- sam: open regression issue with perf numbers and attach traces (I'll do this now)
- anya: collect KV cache timer traces across runs and paste into the issue

infra-bot: Deploy pipeline job queued: `perf/repro-chat/2167778888` — logs will appear here when runs finish.

sam: Opening issue: https://redwood.internal/issues/4853 (perf/regression/multi-gpu-autopick) — added labels: perf, runtime, priority/p1.
leo: Quick note — if kernel choice is sensitive to seq_len distribution, we might need to include a weighted utility that accounts for comm latency (measured via a small microbenchmark) not just peak GFLOPS.
tess: Agreed. I can prototype a tiny utility that runs a few microbatches and reports comm/compute overlap score for candidate kernels.
anya: Great. For now let's keep autoselect disabled on the canary channel until we confirm fix. :thumbsup:
sam: Thanks all — will post results and link traces in the issue.
leo: I'll push a logging PR shortly.
anya: Appreciate it.
